idiom_name: collection interface (add/remove/find) + mapper-backed implementation + flush delegated to the unit of work
implementation_notes: Define one interface per aggregate root exposing collection semantics: add/remove, find by identity, and domain-language queries that take criteria objects rather than SQL text. Implement it against the data mapper or ORM session for loading and storing, and leave flush and commit to the unit of work so the repository never commits a partial operation. Return domain objects or collections of them; never expose query builders, expression trees or row types across the interface, and keep mapping (row to object) inside the implementation. Where the runtime or framework already hands over such a surface (EF Core DbSet, Spring Data repositories, Slick TableQuery, an ActiveRecord relation), use it directly and add only the domain-facing methods the aggregate needs.
code_sketch:
interface InvoiceRepository:                       # one per aggregate root
    add(invoice)                                      # collection semantics
    remove(invoice)
    find_by_id(invoice_id) -> Invoice | None
    find_overdue(on_date) -> list[Invoice]            # domain language, criteria objects

class SqlInvoiceRepository(InvoiceRepository):
    def __init__(self, uow): self._uow = uow          # session / mapper / unit of work
    def find_overdue(self, on_date):
        return [self._mapper.to_domain(r) for r in self._uow.query(OVERDUE_SQL, on_date)]
    # no commit here: the unit of work owns flush and transaction boundaries
pitfalls: Letting the interface grow a method per query turns it into a query builder; factor composable criteria into Query Objects or Specifications instead.
Calling flush/commit inside repository methods splits one business operation into several transactions.
Returning row types, DTOs or lazy query objects across the interface defeats the collection abstraction and leaks persistence into callers.
An in-memory test double that ignores ordering, uniqueness or null semantics hides exactly the bugs the repository was meant to isolate.

Exposing IQueryable or equivalent expression trees across the interface: callers write queries that execute lazily at enumeration time, making query cost invisible and coupling callers to the ORM's expression model.

Generic IRepository<T> with a find_all(predicate) that returns IEnumerable<T> or List<T>: every caller constructs filter logic inline, scattering query intent across the codebase and duplicating the query builder the pattern was meant to eliminate.
Adding business logic (place_order, register_user) into repository methods: business operations belong in domain or application services; repositories should only add, remove, find, and persist.

Wrong move: wrap EF Core DbContext in a generic IRepository<T> for every table -> the wrapper duplicates the framework surface and hides useful queries -> instead expose an aggregate-specific interface only when it protects invariants or a meaningful boundary.

Wrong move: let repository methods accept a transaction or call commit -> independent callers leak or split the transaction boundary -> instead share a unit of work/session and let the application service frame commit and rollback.

Wrong move: route dashboard joins and projections through an aggregate repository -> the interface grows and over-fetches domain objects -> instead use a dedicated CQRS/read-model query path for presentation reads.
